unit:canonical-planning-cutover.title: Canonical productive-planning cutover
unit:canonical-planning-cutover.objective: Integrate daemon-owned canonical planning, deterministic verification, direct compilation, legacy retirement and regression-gate preservation without creating a parallel representation.

outcomes.statement: The integrated proposal defines the daemon as owner of one canonical PlanningEngine, verifier and direct compiler route.
The integrated proposal removes productive reachability of RecursivePlanner, WorkBreakdown projection and the legacy graph compiler.
The integrated proposal preserves daemon lifecycle ownership, exact repository grounding and prior regression gates.

criteria.statement: The daemon composes the canonical planner, verifier and direct compiler as the only productive planning route.
RecursivePlanner, WorkBreakdown projection and the legacy graph compiler are unreachable from productive planning entrypoints.
Daemon lifecycle ownership, repository grounding and existing gates remain green after cutover.

expectedBenefits: Separately validates daemon composition, planning, verification, compilation, retirement and regression responsibilities.
expectedCosts: Requires explicit artifact and seam integration across the cutover boundary.

integration.objective: Integrate the daemon-owned route and prove its canonical artifact flow, legacy exclusion and regression compatibility on the registered repository view.

unit:daemon-composition.title: Daemon planning composition
unit:daemon-composition.objective: Replace the productive daemon planning route with explicit composition of the canonical PlanningEngine, deterministic verifier and direct compiler while retaining daemon lifecycle ownership and exact repository grounding.

outcomes.statement: The daemon adapter supplies the registered repository view to one explicit canonical planning route and emits its typed planning result for lifecycle adoption.

criteria.statement: The daemon owns and composes the canonical productive planning route.

unit:canonical-planning-engine.title: Canonical PlanningEngine
unit:canonical-planning-engine.objective: Make the canonical PlanningEngine produce the sole SemanticPlan from the registered goal, proof obligations and repository view with typed attributable planning failures.

outcomes.statement: Planning generation, canonicalization and deterministic selection yield only the canonical SemanticPlan representation for downstream verification and compilation.

criteria.statement: The canonical PlanningEngine is the sole productive plan producer.

unit:deterministic-verifier.title: Deterministic SemanticPlan verifier
unit:deterministic-verifier.objective: Enforce deterministic SemanticPlan material, criterion-refinement, artifact-flow, seam and resource-ownership checks before direct compilation.

outcomes.statement: A SemanticPlan is either deterministically accepted as compiler input or rejected with typed attributable findings.

criteria.statement: The productive route applies deterministic verification to the canonical SemanticPlan before compilation.

unit:direct-compiler.title: Direct SemanticPlan compiler
unit:direct-compiler.objective: Compile the verified SemanticPlan directly into one canonical GraphRevision with typed artifacts, seams and resource claims, without a WorkBreakdown projection.

outcomes.statement: The compiler consumes the canonical SemanticPlan and deterministic verification result directly and produces a canonical GraphRevision.

criteria.statement: The productive compiler transforms the canonical SemanticPlan directly into GraphRevision.

unit:legacy-retirement.title: Legacy planning retirement
unit:legacy-retirement.objective: Make RecursivePlanner, WorkBreakdown projection and the legacy graph compiler unreachable from productive planning while preserving an explicit non-productive audit boundary where required.

outcomes.statement: A deterministic productive-entrypoint scan finds no reachable RecursivePlanner, WorkBreakdown projection or legacy graph-compiler route.

criteria.statement: Legacy planning and projection components are unreachable from productive planning entrypoints.

unit:regression-gates.title: Regression gate preservation
unit:regression-gates.objective: Preserve canonical GraphRevision validation invariants and execute the registered prior gates against the cutover candidate without moving lifecycle or planning ownership.

outcomes.statement: Prior lifecycle, repository-grounding and canonical-graph gates validate the exact cutover candidate and retain their negative controls.

criteria.statement: Daemon lifecycle ownership, repository grounding and existing gates remain green after cutover.

seam:daemon-to-planner.specification: The daemon supplies the immutable goal contract and exact registered RepositoryView to the canonical PlanningEngine and retains lifecycle adoption authority.

rules: GoalContract revision and digest must match the registered contract.
RepositoryView digest and treeSha must match the registered view.

seam:planner-to-verifier-and-compiler.specification: The PlanningEngine emits the sole canonical SemanticPlan for deterministic verification and direct compilation.

rules: No WorkBreakdown projection may mediate productive compilation.
SemanticPlan must reference the registered GoalContract and RepositoryView.

seam:verifier-to-compiler.specification: The deterministic verifier provides an attributable verification result that gates direct GraphRevision compilation.

rules: Required validation findings must block compilation.
The verified material digest must identify the compiler input.

seam:compiler-to-integration.specification: The direct compiler provides the canonical GraphRevision candidate to regression validation and root integration.

rules: Artifact, seam and resource relations must remain canonical.
GraphRevision must identify the source SemanticPlan and exact RepositoryView.

seam:legacy-to-integration.specification: Legacy retirement supplies static reachability evidence to root integration.

rules: The protected negative control must detect a reintroduced legacy reference.
The scan must cover productive daemon planning entrypoints.

seam:regression-to-integration.specification: Regression validation supplies prior-gate results for the exact integrated candidate.

rules: Evidence must identify the exact candidate under integration.
Lifecycle ownership and repository-view checks must remain included.

advisoryFindings.message: The registered RepositoryView is partial, so implementation-time validation must resolve each pre-registered command against the exact candidate without treating uninspected repository areas as positive evidence.
